reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: One of the two forms of multiple carboxylase deficiency; the neonatal/early-onset form, caused by biallelic HLCS variants
Holocarboxylase synthetase attaches biotin to the four biotin-dependent carboxylases, so deficiency impairs all of them simultaneously
Typically presents in the neonatal period with feeding difficulties, lethargy, hypotonia, seizures and severe metabolic acidosis
Cutaneous features (erythematous rash, alopecia) and ketolactic acidosis with hyperammonaemia are characteristic
Urine organic acids show a combined pattern: 3-hydroxyisovalerate, 3-methylcrotonylglycine, methylcitrate, propionate and lactate
Distinguished from biotinidase deficiency, which usually presents later; both are biotin-responsive multiple carboxylase deficiencies
Most patients respond well to oral biotin supplementation, though very severe HLCS variants can be partially responsive
Confirm by enzyme studies or HLCS sequencing; treat acute crises with fluids, glucose and correction of acidosis alongside biotin
reference.pathophysiology: Holocarboxylase synthetase covalently links biotin to the apoenzymes of the four biotin-dependent carboxylases: pyruvate carboxylase, propionyl-CoA carboxylase, 3-methylcrotonyl-CoA carboxylase and acetyl-CoA carboxylase. When the enzyme is deficient, biotinylation fails and all four carboxylases lose activity, disrupting gluconeogenesis, amino acid (leucine, isoleucine, valine) and odd-chain fatty acid catabolism, and fatty acid synthesis. The result is accumulation of lactate, organic acids and ammonia, producing a severe ketolactic metabolic acidosis with hyperammonaemia and multiorgan dysfunction. Because the biochemical defect is in biotin utilisation rather than an absolute lack of the vitamin, pharmacological biotin can drive residual holocarboxylase synthetase activity and restore carboxylase function in most cases. Inheritance is autosomal recessive.
additionalDifferentials: Biotinidase deficiency (the late-onset multiple carboxylase deficiency)
Isolated propionic, methylmalonic or isovaleric acidaemia
Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency and primary lactic acidoses
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids showing the combined carboxylase-deficiency pattern
Plasma acylcarnitine profile (raised 3-hydroxyisovaleryl and propionyl species)
Blood gas, lactate, glucose and ammonia during crises
Serum biotinidase activity to differentiate biotinidase deficiency
HLCS gene sequencing or fibroblast carboxylase/enzyme studies
Plasma amino acids to assess for secondary elevations
Trial of and response to oral biotin as supportive evidence
redFlags: Severe ketolactic acidosis with cardiovascular instability in the neonate
Significant hyperammonaemia during an acute crisis
Rapidly progressive skin breakdown with secondary infection
Poor or delayed biotin response indicating a severe variant
reference.prognosis: Most patients respond dramatically to biotin supplementation with resolution of the metabolic and cutaneous features and good long-term outcome, but severely affected neonates with poorly responsive variants may sustain neurological damage or die if treatment is delayed.
pitfalls: Not starting a biotin trial promptly in an acidotic neonate with a suggestive organic acid pattern
Confusing HLCS deficiency with the later-presenting biotinidase deficiency and mismanaging follow-up
Attributing the rash to a primary dermatological or nutritional condition
Assuming full biotin responsiveness in every case, missing partially responsive severe variants
Overlooking hyperammonaemia and lactic acidosis as reversible contributors to encephalopathy
references: Scriver's Online Metabolic and Molecular Bases of Inherited Disease (OMMBID)
Saudubray, Inborn Metabolic Diseases: Diagnosis and Treatment
management: Institute lifelong pharmacological oral biotin supplementation, the disease-specific treatment that restores carboxylase activity and reverses the metabolic and cutaneous features
Manage acute metabolic crises with intravenous fluids and dextrose, correction of metabolic acidosis, and ammonia-lowering measures, using dialysis for severe hyperammonaemia
Provide supportive skin care for the erythematous rash and alopecia, which resolve with biotin
Monitor urine organic acids, plasma acylcarnitines, blood gas, lactate and ammonia to confirm biochemical response and guide biotin dosing
Implement sick-day rules with early presentation and avoidance of catabolism during intercurrent illness
Refer to a metabolic medicine team and specialist dietitian for ongoing management
Offer genetic counselling and family testing given autosomal recessive inheritance, and consider sibling and prenatal testing
